headline: Council opens consultation on a city centre access levy
text: Ashcombe Borough Council has opened a twelve-week consultation on a proposed city centre access levy. No charge level is proposed at this stage. Officers say any scheme would need cabinet approval before a vote.

headline: Consultation closes with 61 percent opposed
text: The access levy consultation drew 4,180 responses, of which 61 percent opposed the scheme outright. Opposition was concentrated among residents of the outer wards who commute inward by car.

headline: Draft proposal puts the levy at 4.50 pounds a day
text: The draft scheme published today models a daily charge of 4.50 pounds for non-exempt vehicles. Officers note the figure is illustrative and that exemptions for blue badge holders and trades vehicles remain unresolved.

headline: Committee delays the levy decision to spring
text: The transport committee has deferred its decision on the access levy, citing unresolved questions about exemptions and enforcement costs. No new date has been set beyond an intention to return in spring.

headline: Memo suggests a phased rollout is under consideration
text: An internal memo seen by this office suggests officers are modelling a phased rollout, with the outer ring introduced later than the core zone. The memo is not a proposal and carries no charge level.

headline: Council schedules the access levy vote
text: A date has been set for the full council vote on the access levy. Papers will be published in advance of the meeting.

headline: The access levy explained
text: The Ashcombe access levy charges 7.50 pounds a day for non-exempt vehicles entering the core zone. Blue badge holders and registered trades vehicles are exempt.

headline: Questions raised over the levy rollout
text: Councillor Rowe has faced sustained questions over the handling of the rollout, including the decision to defer enforcement in the outer ring.

headline: Council approves the access levy at 7.50 pounds
text: Full council has approved the city centre access levy at 7.50 pounds a day, well above the 4.50 pounds modelled in the draft. The scheme starts on 1 October 2024.

headline: Access levy goes live, early traffic down 17.8 percent
text: The access levy took effect on 1 October 2024. Cordon counts in the first fortnight show inbound traffic down 17.8 percent against the same period last year.

headline: Councillor Rowe resigns over the levy rollout
text: Councillor Rowe has resigned from the transport committee following criticism of the access levy rollout and the deferred enforcement decision in the outer ring.
